The core similarity of changing the price by $0 (resulting in a $12 final price) is that it represents a maximal assertion of self-interest and a refusal to give the broker any share of the potential bonus. This is comparable to an individual or company that demands the full, non-negotiable price for their service or product, effectively telling the intermediary or reseller they must make their profit elsewhere, or simply confirming their role as a necessary, but unpaid, facilitator. By setting the price at $12, you ensure that in the bonus scenario, you receive the maximum possible bonus ($12), while the broker receives zero ($\$12 - \$12 = \$0$), demonstrating a non-collaborative or transactional stance toward the partnership.
